engine_name: Fitness Age: HUNT non-exercise VO₂peak model (Nes 2011; men 100.27 − 0.296 age + 0.226 PA − 0.369 waist − 0.155 RHR; women 74.736 − 0.247 age + 0.198 PA − 0.259 waist − 0.114 RHR), HUNT activity index (frequency × intensity × duration), and a transparent fitness-age definition on the model's own age slope against a reference person (waist 94 cm men / 80 cm women, resting HR 70, activity index 3.75), clamped 18–90 and rounded half-up (D3-26)
intended_use: Estimates VO₂peak (1 dp) with the age-and-sex band, shows the age at which the reference person of the same sex has that VO₂peak, and shows how activity, resting heart rate and waist can improve it. An estimate from a questionnaire, not a fitness test. Premium, signed in: the change since the last saved check (FR3-52 AS-02).
eligibility: Adults aged 18 to 99 (model derived 20–90; 18–19 use the equation and get a note). Sex 'prefer not to say' cannot calculate (D3-27). No result for heart-rate-lowering medicine Yes or Not sure; not suitable for a declared heart condition, pregnancy or breastfeeding; under 18 stops. Waist lever hidden with an eating-disorder answer or flag.
sources: Nes BM, Janszky I, Vatten LJ, Nilsen TIL, Aspenes ST, Wisløff U. Estimating VO2peak from a nonexercise prediction model: the HUNT Study, Norway. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2011;43:2024–30 (PMID 21502897; abstract verified on Europe PMC: 4,637 participants, final models 2,067 men and 2,193 women, R² 0.61 / 0.56, SEE 5.70 / 5.14).

Peterman JE, et al. J Am Heart Assoc 2020;9:e015117 (PMC7428991), Table 1: the independent reproduction of the Nes 2011 coefficients used by this sheet (its footnote mislabels RHR as 'respiratory exchange ratio'; the text and Table 2 use resting heart rate).
Nes BM, et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2014;46:1159–65 (validation for mortality prediction).
Kurtze N, et al. Reliability and validity of the HUNT physical activity questions. BMC Med Res Methodol 2008;8:63 (activity index).
Loe H, et al. PLoS One 2013;8:e64319 (HUNT reference tables; considered for option C, not used).
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021), fitness norms (age-and-sex band).
limitations: An estimate from a questionnaire, not a fitness test (±5–6 VO₂ points for most people; SEE 5.70 men, 5.14 women).
For healthy adults; medicines that slow the heart make it inaccurate, so no result is shown with a heart-rate-lowering medicine.
Not for heart conditions, pregnancy or breastfeeding; the model was derived in adults aged 20–90.
'Fitness age' is not defined in Nes 2011; the site's definition is the model's age slope against a reference person (D3-26), clamped to 18–90.
The coefficients come from one independent reproduction (Peterman et al., JAHA 2020); the paper's own table 3 is paywalled and has not been seen (D3-32).
regulatory_statement: Approved by the owner as clinical reviewer on 3 November 2026 (P3-5A sign-off record, NFR3-14). General information, not a diagnosis, not a medical device.
licence: Lifeline Daily's own implementation of the published Nes 2011 equations and the HUNT activity questions; free to use.
